purpose: Machine-readable index of every claim this repository makes, with its evidence. Validated by test/test-findings.js, which checks the numbers against the same library the suites use, checks that each registering commit precedes its results commit, and checks that each named test file exists and mentions the finding.

outcome_values.HELD: Registered as a prediction before the run, and the run confirmed it.
outcome_values.FAILED: Registered as a prediction before the run, and the run refuted it. Kept, not corrected away.
outcome_values.MEASURED_NOT_REGISTERED: Measured during design rather than predicted. Listed separately so the pre-registration record is not inflated by facts that were never at risk.

prediction_sets.subject: What the TGATE control vocabulary generates

predictions.claim: addi saturates at exactly 3^w
the full control vocabulary saturates rather than growing freely
reach(all, w) = reach(all, 1)^w, a direct product across trit positions
predictions.note: The failure produced the real law. One composition step applies one control to ALL positions, so after d steps every position carries a word of length exactly d; the positions must agree on word LENGTH, which is weaker than a direct product. reach(w) = |union over d of (M_d)^w|, validated on five widths before being used at width 6.

predictions.claim: more controls buy elements here, unlike table-audit's wide16
reach(all, 6) is not 531441
the shift vocabulary saturates

prediction_sets.subject: What TOP buys, once the truth table is data

predictions.claim: TOP with the second operand pinned reaches 27 at every width
predictions.note: 19,683 tables collapse to 27 maps: one column is in play, so every position gets the same map.

predictions.claim: pinned TOP reaches fewer elements than TGATE for width >= 2
TOP with a free second operand reaches exactly 27^w
predictions.note: And it explains why P3 failed: TOP can express the IDENTITY as a column, so positions idle while others advance, dissolving the equal-word-length constraint. TGATE has no identity mode.

predictions.claim: 27^w is the ceiling for any positionwise vocabulary
the width-6 ceiling 27^6 exceeds 531441
the positionwise vocabulary saturates at exactly 27^w
27 more positionwise generators reach the same number
one translation exceeds 27^w at width 2 by at least 10x
one shift also escapes at width 2
the escape is cross-trit coupling, not generator count
predictions.note: Not all coupling is equal, and this was NOT predicted: the carry buys 3,483x what the shift does, because a carry is data-dependent and a shift is a fixed relabelling.

prediction_sets.subject: Folding a chain of TOP tables into one

predictions.claim: an N-stage chain folds to one instruction, saving (N-1) stages
predictions.note: Held, with an accounting correction: S1 was written in STAGES, and each stage is six instructions, so the saving reads as 18-20 instructions rather than 3. The prose in the first run also mis-rendered this line before it was cleaned up.

predictions.claim: the saving multiplies with emulation depth
hash-consing pays exactly 9 cells per duplicate table
the fold does not survive a carry

prediction_sets.subject: TOPC, the carry as a table

predictions.claim: no TOP table equals ADD, over all 19683, compared as functions
predictions.note: The 81 is the point: a single-point comparison would have reported 81 false matches.

predictions.claim: positionwise + TOPC carrying ADD reaches 251505 at width 2
TOPC in the core would end depth 4

prediction_sets.subject: Whether the ceiling ladder has another rung

predictions.claim: at width 1 the carry is inert; TOPC reaches 27 like TOP
at width 2 TOPC alone exceeds the 729 ceiling
arbitrary carries reach more than the 251505 that ADD alone reaches
predictions.note: The first run reported this as FAILED. It had not failed: at depth 16 the sampled vocabulary was still growing while the ADD one had closed, so a smaller number was read as a smaller reach. The auditor now distinguishes closed, capped and depth-exhausted, and a test asserts all three stay distinguishable.

predictions.claim: the sample is a lower bound and no upper bound is claimed

prediction_sets.subject: The switch-level device layer beneath the arithmetic

predictions.claim: six per-trit gates side by side compute the six-trit function, exhaustively
gates compose: a pass network driving a pass network does not degrade
predictions.note: The first run reported this FAILED. The circuit was correct; the SOLVER was wrong -- reachability traversed through rails, so correct circuits resolved to X. Driven nodes are terminals now. Second time an instrument here produced a false verdict on its own prediction; the first was V3.

predictions.claim: at equal representable range the naive switch count favours ternary, and should not be believed
predictions.note: The ternary side taps a third rail this model hands out free; real ternary logic must generate its mid level with dividers that burn static power. Switch count per gate is also a different currency from the 3.08x per-digit bar.

prediction_sets.subject: The axioms the switch-level device model rests on

predictions.claim: the inclusive threshold (D3) is load-bearing: strict thresholds break every gate
predictions.note: The row counts were derived by hand and written into the registration before the run. They were right. On this integer domain a strict n(t) is an inclusive n(t+1), and a device that can never conduct is indistinguishable from an absent one, so the mutation is a transformation of the device list rather than a patch to the solver.

predictions.claim: the fixed point is not unique, and an all-X start is indistinguishable from all-Z
predictions.note: FAILED on its premise, not its answer. It asked which seeds of the self-inverter are self-consistent, taking for granted that every seed resolves to something. Two of three do not: seeded at a level the network runs -1 -> +1 -> -1 forever and solve() throws. That falsified N7, which claimed resolution cannot oscillate, full stop -- true only from the all-Z start, where a node on a gate CYCLE never gets a determined gate and so lands on X and stays. Nodes elsewhere firm up in gate-dependency order and may pass THROUGH X: an earlier wording of the correction said they reach X on the first pass and stay, which is false, and 481 passing checks did not notice because none of them looked at an intermediate pass. One does now. N7 was reworded to say so. The second half of X2 held exactly: 0 of 27 rows differ, because conducts() maps Z and X alike to unknown.

predictions.claim: composition (T3) holds for every wiring, not just the one already tested
the series mid path is not redundant: no single device can replace it

measured.why_six_not_twelve: D4 -- terminals are interchangeable, checked here rather than assumed

predictions.claim: four switches is minimal for NEG in this model
predictions.note: The positive control first reported the standard ternary inverter ABSENT from a search that had in fact found it: the network key ordered its terminals, and D4 says terminals have no order. Third time an instrument here produced a false verdict on its own prediction. V3 and W2 were the others.

prediction_sets.subject: The carry cell and the six-trit adder, built out of switches

predictions.claim: the assembled six-trit ripple adder is T.add, exhaustively, including the overflow trit
predictions.note: The carry-out was part of the claim on purpose. Without it the circuit is a mod-729 unit rather than an adder, and a sweep that ignored it would pass on a circuit that silently discards overflow.

predictions.claim: every pair settles in exactly seven passes, never six, whatever the carry does
predictions.note: Derived before the run rather than probed: reachability is transitive closure, so a fully determined chain of switches resolves in ONE pass however long it is, and staging happens only where a gate is still unknown. Cell 0 resolves on pass 1, cell i on pass i+1, and pass 7 observes nothing changed. Ripple delay is invisible to a model with no delays in it -- the single cost a ripple adder is famous for is the one this model cannot show. Five hand-picked pairs had been checked during design; 531,441 is what made it a result.

predictions.claim: sharing identical leaf selectors does not break the circuit
predictions.note: Registered as the most likely of the five to fail. A shared leaf ties two mid-level selectors to one node, so the shared circuit contains conducting paths BETWEEN mid nodes that the tree structure did not have -- identical tables do not in general imply identical circuits, and a pass network is where that distinction bites. Here they did.

predictions.claim: and sharing does not change the settling depth
the cost reversal against W3 is structural, not an artefact of six trits against ten bits
predictions.note: W3 measured 0.80 for MIN and predicted it should not be believed. Both numbers are real and the currency did not change: MIN is positionwise, so six wide slices beat ten narrow ones, while an adder is a table and a selector tree over three inputs is 3^3 wide in ternary against 2^3 in binary. The per-digit saving is spent on tree width. The binary adder compared against was itself checked exhaustively at five bits, because a cost comparison against a circuit that does not work is not a comparison.

prediction_sets.subject: The two limits every switch count in this repository was quoted under

predictions.claim: the free mid rail is load-bearing for exactly one published result, and it is the one that favoured ternary
predictions.note: T5 says the generator cannot be built inside the model at all: a divider between vss and vdd is two rails reaching one node, which is contention. So this break-even is a charge from outside the vocabulary rather than a circuit that could be drawn here. What can be said exactly is how dear it would have to be, and twelve switches is not dear.

predictions.claim: buffering cannot take ternary pass depth below 4, and binary gets 3 for free
predictions.note: FAILED on its conclusion, not its numbers. The buffered floors are exactly as registered: 6 -> 4 -> 4 ternary and 3 -> 2 -> 2 binary. What failed is the clause that followed -- that 4 is the best depth ternary can buy AT ANY PRICE. Nothing measured quantified over designs; it quantified over where buffers go inside one family of selector trees. Decode the select instead of gating on it: a four-switch detector pulls to vss for LOW and HIGH and passes vmid for MID, paid once per select signal rather than once per selector, and then every selector arm is a single device including the middle one. The decoded adder cell reaches depth 3 -- equal to binary unrestored -- at 90 switches against 104, so it is shallower AND cheaper than the design the floors were measured on. Third time a clause in this repository outran its measurement; P3 and X2 were the others. Kept as FAILED, and the refutation is checked in test/test-midrail.js.

predictions.claim: what restoration costs, at each level of it
predictions.note: Restoring makes the ratio worse, not better, and increases the mid-rail tap count rather than reducing it. Buffering both levels costs nearly double buffering one and buys no depth at all on either side, because the cheaper option already reaches both floors.

predictions.claim: the restored circuits still add
predictions.note: At risk because a restoring buffer is an inverter driven BY a pass network and driving another one, which is the exact arrangement stated limit 2 handles by assumption. If that assumption were doing work, this is where it would have shown.

predictions.claim: restoration costs passes, and that is the only way delay appears in this model
predictions.note: All six counts were derived by hand before the run from gate-dependency depth: each inverter is its own stage, so a two-inverter buffer adds two per level, times the number of digits, plus the pass that observes nothing changed. Still independent of the data, exactly as Y2 found for the unrestored circuit. Depth here is structural, never arithmetic.

prediction_sets.subject: The decoded-selector adder — the circuit that failed Z2, at full width

predictions.claim: the decoded six-trit ripple is T.add, exhaustively, including the overflow trit
predictions.note: At risk in a way the selector tree was not: the carry feeds a DETECTOR as well as three raw arms, so cell i depends on cell i-1 through two paths that have to agree. They do. test-decoded.js also checks the two adders against EACH OTHER rather than both against T.add -- different primitives, same function on every sampled pair. The first sweep skipped the correctness check for any pair that did not settle inside the predicted budget, so this result was conditional on that bucket being empty. It is measured now: zero pairs need more than thirteen passes, and every one of the 531,441 was compared.

predictions.claim: 540 switches, and 360 with leaves shared

measured.decomposition: 18 detectors x 4, plus 12 trees x 13 selectors x 3

predictions.claim: read depth 3 for the whole ripple, not just one cell
predictions.note: Half the selector tree, and equal to the binary adder unrestored. The chain resets at every gate and a carry is read as a gate, which is why six cells are no deeper than one.

predictions.claim: exactly 13 passes for every operand pair, still independent of the data
predictions.note: FAILED on universality, not on arithmetic. Thirteen is correct as the WORST case, which is what the derivation actually bounded; the range is 9 to 13 and it DEPENDS ON THE OPERANDS. First circuit in the repository whose settling time is arithmetic rather than structural, and it scoped Y2 and Z5. Their independence-of-data result is a property of gating every arm on the RAW select, which makes all conduction known at one instant so nothing can settle early. Decoding splits the gating across two dependency levels: with the carry-in LOW the LOW arm already conducts while the MID arm gate is still unknown, so if both arms lead to the same rail the node is determined a pass early, by N3. Six of the carry table nine leaves have their LOW and MID cells equal; none of the sum table do. The three outcomes were separated on a second run: 279,936 settle in fewer than thirteen, 251,505 in exactly thirteen, and 0 in more. So 128 of every 243 settle early, and thirteen is a genuine ceiling rather than merely the predicted number. The count is no longer unexplained: the F set derives it exactly. The six agreeing carry leaves enable the saving, and the sum tree never being early is what decides which positions can use it.

predictions.claim: it narrows the gap without closing it, and taps the mid rail less
predictions.note: The ratio half held exactly: 1.93 and 1.64, never below 1.36 at any width from one trit to six, and 3.21x per digit against a log2(3) break-even of 1.585. The mid-rail half was BACKWARDS. The decoded design taps vmid 186 times against 168 -- one more per detector, eighteen of them -- because each detector reaches vmid through its own series pair. So the design that wins on switch count does it partly by leaning harder on the rail Z1 established that nobody is charging for. Kept as FAILED on the X2 precedent: a prediction with a refuted half is not trimmed to the half that survived.

prediction_sets.subject: Where 128/243 comes from — the decoded adder’s pass count, derived

predictions.claim: the rule is exact pair by pair, not merely in aggregate

measured.rule: at carry-in 0: passes = (2n+1) - #{ i in 1..n-2 : c_i != 0 and carry(s_i + c_i) == carry(s_i) }
measured.scope: carry-in 0 throughout; with a non-zero carry-in the bottom position can save as well (six of its nine digit-pairs qualify) and the walk is a different one

predictions.note: Reproducing a total is much weaker than reproducing it term by term, so this was registered in the strong form. Zero disagreements against the actual solver over 597,861 pairs across five widths, every one of them exhaustive. The distribution sums to 531,441. Scoped to carry-in 0 after the fact: every sweep fixed it, and the exclusion of the bottom position is a property of that choice rather than of the circuit. Caught by asking what the sweep actually visited, which is T-CLAIM-NARROWED-BY-A-DESIGN checking itself.

predictions.claim: the sum tree can never settle early, and that asymmetry is the whole result
predictions.note: Early settling needs the arm conducting on the raw select and the arm still waiting on the MID detector to lead to the same rail. For the carry tree that is carry(s+c) == carry(s), true for 12 of 18, because the carry function is flat over stretches. For the sum tree it is lowTrit(s+c) == lowTrit(s), true for none of them, because adding one always moves a low trit. So only the carry tree is ever early; the top position SUM is always the last node to move; and a saving at the top position is therefore invisible. That is exactly why the earlier naive count over-predicted by one, always in the same direction.

predictions.claim: the walk over the carry state gives 251,505 exactly
predictions.note: The matrix is derived from the adder own tables inside the check rather than written down, and comes out as nine ways from the middle carry state and three from each end. The 3^5 in the denominator is four constrained positions plus one free top digit.

predictions.claim: and the same walk predicts every other width
predictions.note: Checked against the actual circuit exhaustively at all five widths. A rule fitted to six trits rather than derived would come apart here. It does not.

prediction_sets.subject: Whether 251,505 appearing twice, from unrelated constructions, is anything

predictions.claim: the correspondence dies at the first other parameter, and not narrowly

measured.pairing: monoid width w against an adder of 3w trits

predictions.note: Decisive in the bluntest available way. At width 1 the monoid acts on three points, so the entire space of functions there is 3^3 = 27 and every monoid at that width, whatever its vocabulary, is at most that. Both vocabularies do reach 27 -- at a single position the positionwise maps already give every unary function. The three-trit adder has 729 operand pairs of which 621 settle late. The monoid universe is smaller than the number it would have to match, so the failure is not a wrong value but no room for one.

predictions.claim: and the two families grow at incompatible rates, so they were never one sequence
predictions.note: The recurrence was derived by hand from the transfer matrix characteristic polynomial before the run and reproduces every count to width 12. Its dominant root is irrational, so the adder family multiplies by about 7.37 per step; the monoid multiplies by about 9,315 across the only span where both are computable. Across eleven adder counts and every monoid reach in the manifest, exactly one value coincides -- the one already known.

predictions.claim: the collision is where two exponent sequences cross, once, not a pattern
predictions.note: They differ at the first width and agree at the second. No formula is claimed for how the monoid ceiling grows -- two data points do not determine one, and the question did not need it.

predictions.claim: and collisions of this size are rare here, which is why one looked like something

measured.halves_derived_from: which library each tool imports: monoid-lib or device.js
measured.self_reference_excluded: the censusing set, matched by its tool name

predictions.note: The instrument produced a false verdict first, and this is the fourth time that has happened here. The registration said prediction sets THAT MEASURE DIFFERENT THINGS and the first loop dropped the clause, counting 279,936 as colliding with itself because two sets record the same adder count, and 4,489 likewise because two sets share a sampling stride. Corrected by classifying each set by which library its tool imports -- derived, not hardcoded -- and requiring a collision to cross that line. The disambiguation rule was chosen after the first run, which is a degree of freedom worth declaring; it implements a clause that was in the registration beforehand, and the two excluded values are restatements of one quantity under any reading. Then a second correction, and a better one. Recording this very result put 279,936 and 4,489 into the manifest again -- as the values G4 had just EXCLUDED -- and on the next run they crossed the halves and G4 failed. The measurement had become part of the corpus it measures. A census cannot count the set that is the census; the tool and the test now drop it by matching the censusing tool name rather than an id.

prediction_sets.subject: Whether this model can carry a machine, and what charge retention would cost

predictions.claim: the solver is linear in devices times passes, not superlinear as the design documents assert
predictions.note: FAILED on both registered criteria, and the direction of the failure is the useful part. The exponent came in BELOW 1.0 both times - sublinear, better than predicted - because fixed per-solve overhead dominates the smallest networks and the derivation had no term for it. Above 512 devices, where overhead washes out, the spread is 1.64x and the exponent 1.088: both inside the registered band. Worse, the spread criterion was not reproducible - 3.72 on one run and 2.89 on the next, either side of the line it had been given. A criterion whose verdict depends on run-to-run noise is a defect in the prediction. The claim being tested is nonetheless settled: the solver is not superlinear, and the two documents saying so were corrected. The registration also mis-cited one of those documents as design/04-device-model.md, which is design/04-storage.md; the claim lives in design/10-integration.md, design/11-open.md and two doctree pillars, all four now corrected.

predictions.claim: so the machine is simulatable, and what is lost is sweeping it
predictions.note: The registered output was the crossover, and it is the sharpest thing this set produced: a full 531,441-pair sweep fits inside an hour only up to about 4,800 devices. The six-trit adder is 624 and sits comfortably inside. The machine is ~50,000 and does not. So the machine can be RUN and cannot be SWEPT, which makes it the first subject in this repository that sits outside the exhaustive discipline every other result rests on - and the exhaustibility precondition in METHOD.md stops applying to the thing the method was built to study.

predictions.claim: charge retention changes nothing in the existing corpus

measured.patch: one rule: an isolated node keeps its previous value instead of becoming Z

predictions.note: Zero differences anywhere. Derived before the run and confirmed: every circuit here is solved from a cold all-Z start, and a node with no previous value is Z under either rule. The two semantics can only diverge where a node is driven on one pass and isolated on a later one, which no existing circuit does. The comparison is not vacuous - test-headroom.js shows the two solvers DO differ on a written-then-isolated node, which is the case storage needs.

predictions.claim: and it makes storage nearly free, which is why the decision matters
predictions.note: A single pass gate onto an isolated node writes and holds all three trits. One switch against nineteen, and the 729-word memory drops from 48,114 switches to 4,374 - eleven times, against the five the design phase estimated. Since memory is about 93% of the machine, this is the whole decision, and it costs nothing in the existing corpus by H3. The design documents ranking this change fourth by blast radius and first by leverage were right about the ordering and understated the size.

prediction_sets.subject: Whether four switches is minimal for the MID detector, which the adder pays for eighteen times

predictions.claim: four switches is minimal, for every contract the selector accepts
predictions.note: Reading dmux before the search is what made this worth doing properly. Its middle arm is n(selMid, MID, ...), which conducts iff the detector output is at or above MID, so the CONTRACT is that the output be non-negative exactly at MID -- not the particular table that was built. Four tables satisfy it and only one had ever been considered. Nothing at one, two or three switches computes any of them.

predictions.claim: and the positive control finds the detector already in use
predictions.note: A search that finds nothing proves nothing unless it can find something. Four distinct four-switch networks compute the built contract, the one in use among them -- the same count X5 found for NEG.

predictions.claim: the four contracts all cost the same
predictions.note: So the choice between an n-type and a p-type middle arm is free, and the selector cannot be improved by switching polarity.

predictions.claim: so the decoded adder stands at 540
predictions.note: A negative result, and the arithmetic for the other outcome was registered in advance so it could not be massaged afterwards: a three-switch detector would have taken the adder to 522 and the ratio to 1.864. The detector count of 18 is derived from the netlist rather than assumed.

prediction_sets.subject: A six-trit register at switch level — the first sequential circuit here

predictions.claim: six loop-breaking cells under one enable hold a tryte, exhaustively
predictions.note: At risk because six feedback loops settle inside one solve, and nothing in this project had ever solved a network with more than one loop. N7 is about loops and had surfaced consequences twice that only appeared once state arrived. It did not this time.

predictions.claim: and costs 114 switches built for test, 66 in place
predictions.note: The 48-switch difference is six input buffers, which T5 makes mandatory at any boundary with a primary input. Enable fan-out is free in this model and is the largest thing these numbers hide.

predictions.claim: and does not leak
predictions.note: With hold asserted and the write enable low, sweeping the data over the range moves the stored tryte not at all. Strides are stated in the output rather than quietly chosen.

predictions.claim: and a read in the same solve as a write sees the old value
predictions.note: FAILED, cleanly and in the opposite direction. The mechanism is exact and obvious afterwards: while the write enable is asserted the feedback loop is held OPEN -- that is the whole trick that makes the write possible -- so the cell is driven straight from its input and the seeded value has nothing holding it. S0 is a TRANSPARENT LATCH, not a flip-flop, and a transparent latch is see-through by definition. So master-slave is required and the register file is double what design/05 budgeted. design/11 had already listed this as one of five outcomes that would falsify the plan, which is the design phase working: the consequence was named before the measurement, so it could not be argued with afterwards.

prediction_sets.subject: The master-slave register J4 established was required, and the discipline it needs

predictions.claim: it reads the old value while writing the new
predictions.note: The property J4 measured the single latch to lack. Not automatic that the textbook answer would survive this model: three of the four obvious ways to build the single cell were forbidden by axioms.

predictions.claim: and costs 180 switches built for test, 132 in place
predictions.note: Exactly double the single latch and nothing more. The slave needs no input buffer because its input is the master output, already rail-driven. design/05 had estimated ~228.

predictions.claim: and a full two-phase step moves the value through exactly once
and asserting both phases at once breaks it, in the specific way predicted
predictions.note: With both phases high the structure degenerates to precisely the transparent latch J4 measured. So the non-overlap discipline is load-bearing rather than conventional, and the failure it exists to prevent was produced deliberately rather than assumed. Registering the failure mode alongside the success is the point: a structure that only works under a discipline should be shown breaking when the discipline is dropped, or the discipline reads as superstition.

prediction_sets.subject: An accumulator — the first circuit here that computes and remembers

predictions.claim: one two-phase step computes A + B, for every accumulator value
predictions.note: The sum being right is the lesser half. The register is read by the adder while the adder is computing the register next value, and on none of the 6,561 steps did it stop reading the OLD accumulator. That is K1 property under load, and the whole reason the J4 failure mattered.

predictions.claim: and costs 672 switches
predictions.note: No buffer between adder and register because the sum is already rail-driven, which is the one place T5 does not charge. B needs none either, since it only ever gates selectors.

predictions.claim: and its step cost varies with the data
predictions.note: Inherited from the decoded adder, which E4 measured at 9 to 13 passes depending on its operands. So a machine built on this design has no fixed clock period -- the first consequence in this project that behaves like a property of the computation rather than of the structure.

predictions.claim: and it accumulates across steps
predictions.note: The first computation in this repository carried out by simulated transistors holding their own state between steps, wrapping correctly where the running total leaves the tryte range.

unregistered_findings.claim: ADD equals TOPC with the 27-row addition table, exactly.
An interpreter bug that permutes the emulated semantics has an ORDER, and is invisible at layer counts divisible by it. Order 2 is masked at 2 layers; order 3 at 3.
unregistered_findings.consequence: No single depth is a safe place to test; the acceptance tests compare every depth.

unregistered_findings.claim: Folding buys a level of emulation depth, not just instructions: the unfolded chain is refused at depth 4 and the folded one runs.
TGATE's three modes are not closed under composition: 6 of its 8 two-stage composites are not any TGATE mode. This is why TOP folds and TGATE cannot.
Reading -1/0/+1 as false/unknown/true, MIN, MAX and NEG are exactly the connectives of Kleene's strong three-valued logic. Excluded middle and non-contradiction both fail at unknown.
unregistered_findings.precision: For these three connectives K3 and Lukasiewicz's L3 are identical; they diverge only at implication, which this machine has no operator for.

unregistered_findings.claim: Base 3 is the cheapest integer radix by the radix-economy measure: representing a million values costs 40 in base 2, 39 in base 3, 40 in base 4.

Three-way dispatch beats two-way on the same machine by about half an instruction and a fifth of the code per decision point, and nothing at all when the decision is genuinely binary. Deep dispatch loses outright to an indexed jump: 149 cells against 30.

The top rung of the ladder is 531,441, numerically identical to the source conversation's figure, by coincidence. That figure counted two-stage configurations of 6-trit trytes (729^2); this counts elements of a monoid on 9 points (9^6). Both are 3^12 for unrelated reasons, and the conversation's claim about what it counted remains wrong.
The standard ternary inverter computes NEG on all three inputs; MIN and MAX are correct on all nine rows. Switch counts: STI 4, NTI 2, PTI 2, MIN 8, MAX 8.
unregistered_findings.note: Established while designing the gates, so not registered as a prediction.

unregistered_findings.claim: The standard ternary inverter is not the only four-switch NEG in this model. Exhaustive search finds four distinct networks, and it is one of them.
unregistered_findings.evidence: 148,995 four-switch networks over 42 device types, all solved

unregistered_findings.claim: The sum tree of a balanced-ternary full adder has only three distinct leaf selectors of nine, and the carry tree five, because both depend on a+b rather than on a and b separately.
unregistered_findings.evidence: hash-consing the leaf selectors takes the six-trit adder from 624 switches to 384

unregistered_findings.claim: An input gates a device and terminates a path, but never sources one: a conducting device between an input and a node transfers nothing, and the node is Z. Reachability starts at rails and only at rails.
unregistered_findings.evidence: proved as the second half of T5; no circuit in the repository had ever used an input as a pass terminal, so nothing had depended on it either way

unregistered_findings.claim: The number of operand pairs on which the decoded adder settles in exactly thirteen passes is 251,505 — the same figure the monoid audits found for what positionwise logic plus one carrying ADD reaches at width two. Two different objects counted inside the same 3^12 space, landing on the same six-digit number.
unregistered_findings.evidence: 531,441 minus the 279,936 that settle in fewer passes; the rung is recorded in the U set
unregistered_findings.note: Chased and settled by the G set: a coincidence. The pairing that produces it holds at exactly one parameter value, the two families grow at rates a thousandfold apart, and the two numbers are the only pair in the manifest that collides across the vocabulary and circuit halves of the project.

unregistered_findings.claim: The sum and carry halves of a balanced-ternary adder save in exactly complementary currencies, and for one reason. The low trit WRAPS, so its rows repeat across operand sums -- nine leaf selectors collapse to three -- but its cells never agree within a row, so it can never settle early. The carry STEPS, so its rows never repeat -- five of nine, no collapse -- but it is flat over stretches, so twelve of eighteen cells agree within a row and it settles early constantly.
unregistered_findings.evidence: sum tree 3 distinct rows and 0 of 18 in-row agreements; carry tree 5 distinct rows and 12 of 18
unregistered_findings.note: The same fact about balanced-ternary addition appeared once as the 38 percent area saving in Y3 and once as the pass-count distribution in E4 and F. Wrapping buys area; stepping buys time; neither buys both.

traps_encountered.description: Comparing two functions at a single input and concluding they are equal. Bit the mixed-TGATE test, the folded-vs-unfolded programs, and the TOP-vs-ADD comparison, where 81 of 19,683 tables matched at one pair.

A hardcoded count in a test or a document going stale when the thing it counted grew. The closure test kept passing against an opcode list the source no longer had; test-findings.js miscounted its own prediction sets; and the README stated both a check total and a prediction tally that had drifted. The first two were fixed by deriving them. The third could not be owned by any one suite, because it is the sum of all of them, so run-all.js sums the suites and test-findings.js recomputes the tally.
Writing through a missing label produced an undefined address, so the write silently did nothing. The core interpreter ran with no control register and no complaint.
.fold reading nine cells from a table that was shorter, silently borrowing whatever followed it.

Confusing ran out of budget with finished. A search that exhausts its depth limit, one that hits its size cap, and one that genuinely closes are three different outcomes; conflating them produced a false negative verdict on V3. It recurred in the E sweep, where one counter held both settled-sooner-than-predicted and needed-longer-than-predicted, and the correctness check was skipped for the second bucket -- so an exhaustive claim was published while resting on an unmeasured decomposition. That time the numbers happened to be right: the second bucket was empty. Report the outcomes separately and check that they sum to the total.

Switch-level reachability traversing THROUGH a driven node. A path from one rail that touches another rail and continues out of it makes correct circuits look contended. Rails and inputs are ideal sources and must terminate a path.

The measuring tool, not the thing measured, producing the failure. V3 read depth exhaustion as saturation; W2 traversed reachability through rails; X5 keyed a network by ordered terminals when D4 says terminals have no order; G4 dropped a qualifier that was present in its own registration and counted a quantity restated in a second set as colliding with itself. Each reported a verdict about the world that was a fact about the instrument. When a result contradicts a prediction, suspect the instrument first, and check the loop against the sentence that was registered.

A prediction failing on an assumption it never stated rather than on the quantity it asked about. X2 asked which seeds are self-consistent and assumed every seed resolves; two do not. The assumption, not the answer, was the falsifiable part.

A sampling instrument that was not sampling. A seeded generator multiplied a 31-bit seed by a 31-bit constant, which overflows the 53 bits a JS number holds exactly, so the low-order bits it returned were rounding noise: three of its eight node names were drawn essentially never and no random network ever floated or contended. It looked like 400 trials and was closer to 400 repetitions of one. Random input needs a vacuity check on what it actually produced, not on how many times it ran.

A consistency check that treated a legitimate intermediate state as a defect. It demanded that tools/ and the manifest prediction sets be equal in number; they are equal only between phases, because registering a tool predictions and recording its results are deliberately separate commits. During a registration there is one more tool than there are sets, and that is the protocol working. The check now names the pending tool instead of failing on it.

An instrument that searched for a value it could have verified. Finding the exact pass count by scanning k = 1 upward cost up to eighty solves per input on a 1,776-switch network and did not finish inside ten minutes. The count is the same for every input, so it needs finding once and checking twice thereafter -- settles at k, does not settle at k-1. Two solves, not eighty.

A measured result stated as a property of the SUBJECT when it was a property of the DESIGN measured. Z2 swept buffer placements in one family of trees and concluded a depth floor for ternary at any price; a different selector beat it. E4, and Y2 and Z5 before it, measured raw-select circuits and concluded settling time is never data-dependent; a decoded selector made it data-dependent. Both times the numbers were right and the noun was too big. Before writing ternary, or this model, ask whether the sweep visited more than one design.

A measurement over a corpus that the measurement is then written into. G4 surveyed the manifest for repeated integers, and recording its own result added those integers to the manifest a second time -- as the values it had excluded -- so the next run found them colliding and the prediction failed against its own record. Nothing was wrong with the world or the first answer. If a result is stored where it will later be read as data, exclude the storing record from the read, and derive the exclusion from something structural rather than an id.

A registered criterion whose verdict depends on run-to-run variation. H1 predicted a spread under 3x and measured 3.72 on one run and 2.89 on the next, either side of its own line, so the same world produced both a pass and a fail. The attempt to salvage a more robust shape from it flipped too. A threshold placed near the noise floor is a defect in the prediction rather than a fact about the subject; either widen it until it cannot flip, or measure the quantity and report it without asserting a bound.
